description: Production health model for the beta validation agent (deploy/beta-agent/agent.py, the signed POST /provision listener on :8791). DESIGN ONLY — not wired to any runtime. This models the AGENT LISTENER's health, which is distinct from (a) per-account broker health (reliability/broker_health, WP3) and (b) per-validation pipeline stages (trading/validation_timeline). The agent can be HEALTHY while individual validations fail at the host/MT5/broker layer (that is DEGRADED, not agent-unavailable).

probe_chain.signal: :8791 is in LISTEN on the expected private bind
probe_chain.source: OS TCP table / connect probe from the backend (the only firewall-allowed source)

probe_chain.signal: a signed NEGOTIATE handshake returns a compatible contract
probe_chain.source: backend mgmt_client.assert_compatible() — the ONLY health probe the agent exposes (no unauthenticated /health by design)

probe_chain.signal: VALIDATE_LOGIN is advertised in supported_operations and the signing keyring is provisioned
the task-launched runner can bring up MT5 local IPC (validation_ipc_unavailable rate low)
probe_chain.source: validation attempt outcomes / diagnostics — exercised, not continuously probed

probe_chain.signal: broker login completes when reached (server_unavailable/login_timeout rate low)
the backend receives a structured result (not a transport unreachable/timeout)

states.name: STARTING
states.meaning: process launched; binding + first readiness not yet confirmed
states.exit: socket_listening AND negotiate_ok  ->  HEALTHY;  bind/config failure  ->  UNAVAILABLE

transitions.when: readiness probe (through negotiate_ok) passes within start-timeout
bind fails (wrong/public address), config/keyring missing, or start-timeout exceeded

states.operator_action: none while within start-timeout; if exceeded, gather evidence (bind address, config, WinSW/agent log) per the restart runbook

states.name: HEALTHY
states.meaning: process running, socket listening, NEGOTIATE compatible, VALIDATE_LOGIN available; validations succeed or fail only at expected low rates
states.exit: any readiness layer fails, elevated downstream failure rate, or an operator stop

transitions.when: downstream failure rate (IPC/MT5/broker) breaches threshold over the window while NEGOTIATE still succeeds
process exits, socket stops listening, or NEGOTIATE/transport fails (connect timeout / no response)
an operator/supervisor initiates a controlled stop

states.name: DEGRADED
states.meaning: agent is UP and answering NEGOTIATE, but validations are failing at an elevated rate at a downstream layer (host IPC, MT5, or broker). NOT an agent-down condition.
states.entry: failure-rate threshold breached over the rolling window with negotiate_ok still true
states.exit: failure rate recovers to healthy band, or the agent itself stops answering

transitions.when: downstream failure rate returns below the recovery threshold over the window
the agent stops answering NEGOTIATE / socket down

states.operator_action: triage the dominant failure reason via the matching runbook (repeated IPC / repeated MT5 / repeated broker); DO NOT restart on downstream failures alone — a restart does not fix a broker/host-IPC condition and destroys in-flight evidence

states.name: UNAVAILABLE
states.meaning: process not running, OR socket not listening, OR NEGOTIATE/transport fails. Customers see validation_agent_unreachable/validation_agent_timeout.
states.exit: an operator (re)starts the agent via the supported mechanism

transitions.when: an operator starts a controlled restart after an UNEXPECTED unavailable
a supervised auto-restart or planned start begins

states.operator_action: run the 'Agent unavailable' runbook: gather evidence FIRST (service state, listener, last logs, last diagnostics), then start via the supported service mechanism (never an interactive-SSH launch — security RULE 1)

states.name: STOPPING
states.meaning: controlled stop/drain in progress (operator or supervisor)
states.exit: in-flight MUTATING ops drain (RuntimeLockManager); the process then exits
states.drain_boundary: IMPORTANT (adversarial lens 1): the current agent drain (AgentServer.stop -> _await_drain) waits ONLY on the per-runtime mutation lock. The credentialed VALIDATE_LOGIN uses its OWN global single-flight lock and is NOT covered by that drain — a stop mid-login FORCE-CUTS a ~165s (login_timeout_ms + cleanup_grace) credentialed login; the runner destroys the decrypted credential out-of-band (its own finally/cleanup), but the agent-level 'clean drain' does NOT apply to it. Hardening (RR-1a): wire the login validator into the drain (deny new logins during drain; wait out the in-flight login up to a stoptimeout that exceeds login_timeout_ms+grace).
states.operator_action: verify the mutation drain completed; be aware an in-flight VALIDATE_LOGIN is force-cut on stop (credential cleanup is runner-side, not an agent drain) until RR-1a lands

states.name: RECOVERY
states.entry: an operator starts the agent after an unexpected exit
states.exit: NEGOTIATE succeeds -> HEALTHY; fails again -> UNAVAILABLE (escalate)

transitions.when: readiness passes after restart and stays stable for the confirm window
readiness fails again within the confirm window (crash loop -> escalate)

states.operator_action: follow the restart runbook; capture the exit evidence BEFORE restart; if it re-fails within the confirm window, escalate (do not loop restarts)

invariants: Every non-terminal state defines at least one transition.
Every transition target is a defined state.
A downstream (MT5/broker/IPC) failure moves HEALTHY->DEGRADED, never HEALTHY->UNAVAILABLE (the agent is still up).
UNAVAILABLE is only entered from a readiness-layer failure (process/socket/negotiate) or an intended STOPPING exit.
No state auto-restarts without an explicit supervised policy (today: none; see readiness-review).
